rationale: The strongest candidate is P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency caching). The measured Gradle experiment (batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200) showed about 20% elapsed savings from adding actions/cache for ~/.gradle/caches. However, this workflow already enables Gradle dependency caching via `cache: gradle` in actions/setup-java@v6, so an equivalent cache already exists, which is a listed contraindication for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE. Adding a duplicate actions/cache step would be redundant and is not supported. No other pattern fits: there is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST/P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE not applicable), no representative successful-duration history to set a safe custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT contraindicated), and the shared Gradle build configuration makes path-based change filtering risky for required checks (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER contraindicated). Build and test coverage (./gradlew build plus Jacoco/Codacy reporting) is preserved unchanged.
